facts.value: In 1959, statistician Theodore Sterling examined the results of psychological studies and found that 97% supported their initial hypotheses, suggesting possible publication bias.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Similarly, Fanelli (2010) found that 91.5% of psychiatry/psychology studies confirmed the effects they were looking for, concluding that the odds of this happening (a positive result) was around five times higher than in fields such as space science or geosciences.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Fanelli argued that this is because researchers in 'softer' sciences have fewer constraints on their conscious and unconscious biases.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick
